add-text-to-pdf.formula:
x = (horizontal % ÷ 100) × page width − text width ÷ 2
y = (vertical % ÷ 100) × page height
(preset spots subtract a 36 pt margin from the matching edge)
howTo: Click “Choose PDF file” and select the document you want to stamp.
Type the text — a name, a “DRAFT” watermark, a signature line, anything up to 500 characters.
Choose whether the text goes on every page or on one specific page.
Pick one of the nine preset positions, or use the custom option for exact placement.
Set the font size, color and rotation, then click “Add text” and download the result.
keyFacts: The text is drawn directly into the page content with the standard Helvetica font, so it looks identical in every PDF reader.
PDF pages use a point-based grid: an A4 page is 595.28 × 841.89 points, with (0, 0) at the bottom-left corner.
Preset positions measure a 36-point (half-inch) margin from the matching page edges.
Custom placement uses percentages of the page size, so the same settings work on A4, Letter and mixed-size documents.
Rotation is measured in degrees around the text start point: 45 gives a classic diagonal watermark.

add-text-to-pdf.workedExample:
Stamp “DRAFT” at middle-center of an A4 page (595.28 × 841.89 pt), 48 pt, rotated 0°:
text width ≈ 5 characters × 24 pt ≈ 120 pt
x = (595.28 − 120) ÷ 2 = 237.64 pt from the left edge
y = 841.89 ÷ 2 = 420.95 pt from the bottom edge
The word lands perfectly centered on the page.
